chapter: Continuity of Life: Cell Division and Reproduction
trick: Mitosis copies, meiosis halves. Mitosis makes two cells identical to the parent for growth and repair; meiosis makes four cells with half the chromosomes, for gametes. Count the products and the chromosome number and you can never confuse them.

video.query: mitosis meiosis stages prophase metaphase anaphase telophase class 10 biology

data.prompt: Put the stages of mitosis into the order they happen.

items.label: Interphase
items.note: The cell grows and the DNA is copied; not part of division proper

items.label: Prophase
items.note: Chromosomes condense and become visible; the nuclear membrane starts to break down

items.label: Metaphase
items.note: Chromosomes line up along the equator of the cell

items.label: Anaphase
items.note: Sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite poles

items.label: Telophase
items.note: Two new nuclear membranes form around the separated sets

items.label: Cytokinesis
items.note: The cytoplasm divides and two daughter cells exist

trick: Draw the Punnett square every time, even when you think you know. Two minutes of grid beats a guessed ratio, and the two ratios worth knowing by heart are 3:1 for a monohybrid cross and 9:3:3:1 for a dihybrid.

video.query: Mendel monohybrid cross Punnett square 3:1 ratio class 10 life science

data.prompt: Work a monohybrid cross through, one step at a time.
data.problem: A tall pea plant (TT) is crossed with a dwarf one (tt). The F1 plants are then self-pollinated. What is the ratio of tall to dwarf plants in the F2 generation?

steps.ask: What are the genotypes of the F1 plants?
steps.why: Each parent can give only one kind of gamete, T from TT and t from tt, so every F1 plant must be Tt.

steps.ask: So what do all the F1 plants look like?
steps.why: T is dominant over t, so a Tt plant is tall. The dwarf character has not vanished, only been masked.

steps.ask: Crossing Tt with Tt, what genotypes appear in the F2?
steps.why: The Punnett square of Tt × Tt gives one TT, two Tt and one tt, that is a genotypic ratio of 1:2:1.

steps.ask: What is the ratio of tall to dwarf plants?
steps.why: TT, Tt and Tt are all tall and only tt is dwarf, so three tall to one dwarf. Note the genotypic ratio is 1:2:1 but the phenotypic ratio is 3:1; questions ask for one or the other, so read carefully.

data.answer: 3 tall : 1 dwarf, with an underlying genotypic ratio of 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt.

trick: Nothing evolves because it wants to. Variation comes first, by chance, and the environment then decides which variations survive. Any explanation that has an animal deciding to change is Lamarck's, and Lamarck was wrong.

video.query: evolution Darwin natural selection adaptation class 10 life science

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about evolution.

items.statement: Darwin's theory explains evolution by natural selection acting on existing variation.
items.why: Variation arises first and by chance; the environment then selects. This is the heart of On the Origin of Species, 1859.

items.statement: A giraffe's neck grew long because its ancestors kept stretching for high leaves.
items.why: That is Lamarck's inheritance of acquired characters, which is rejected. Stretching in one lifetime does not change the gametes.

items.statement: Homologous organs have the same basic structure but may do different jobs.
items.why: A human arm, a bat's wing and a whale's flipper share a bone plan, which is evidence of common ancestry.

items.statement: Analogous organs are evidence of common ancestry.
items.why: Analogous organs do the same job with quite different structures, such as an insect's wing and a bird's wing. They show convergent evolution, not shared descent.

items.statement: Fossils are direct evidence for evolution.
items.why: The deeper the layer, the older and usually the simpler the fossil, which shows life changing across time.

trick: In-situ means in its own place, ex-situ means out of it. A national park or a sanctuary protects an animal where it already lives; a zoo, a seed bank or a botanical garden protects it somewhere else. The Latin tells you the answer.
